title: Agent snippet: adj ai and JSON shape docs
lead:
`adj ai` prints a short AGENTS.md snippet telling agents how to use adj, and a
test pins every read command's `--json` shape to `docs/json.md`.
findings_note: PROJECT.md v1 feature tier; Risks (adoption); acceptance (--json documented)
boundary: **Not in this slice:** the user-facing README and the dogfood run.

sections.heading: Why
sections.body:
Risks: agents only use adjudicate if the instruction is short and the commands
are cheap. Acceptance requires a documented, stable `--json` shape on every
read command.

sections.heading: Files
sections.body:
- `internal/commands/ai.go`: the snippet, as a string constant or a file
  embedded with the standard `embed` package (for example
  `internal/commands/ai.md`).
- `internal/cli/ai_test.go`.
- `internal/cli/jsonshape_test.go`.
- `docs/json.md`: completed for `show`, `list`, `inbox`, `check` and `context`.

sections.heading: Failing tests
sections.body:
- `adj ai` exits 0 and prints the snippet.
- The snippet names `adj check`, `adj ask`, `adj inbox` and `adj context`, and
  says that only the owner decides (C27).
- For each of `show`, `list`, `inbox`, `check` and `context`, the top-level
  `--json` keys equal the shape in `docs/json.md`. How the test reads the doc
  (for example one fenced JSON example per command) is an implementer decision
  recorded under C32.

sections.heading: Implement
sections.body:
Write the snippet using the name `adj` (C23), keep it short, and complete
`docs/json.md`. `lint --json` lands later, in S14, which documents its own
shape.

sections.heading: Check
sections.body:
Run from the repo root after `. scripts/env.sh` (the in-repo cache env, C33;
use the equivalent AGENTS.md names if S02 chose another):

- `go test ./...` passes, including this slice's new tests.
- `go vet ./...` reports nothing.
- `gofmt -l cmd internal` prints nothing (not `gofmt -l .`, which also walks
  `.cache/` and `.worktrees/`).
- Each interface choice made in this slice is a slicer catalog decision with a
  one-line reason (C32).
- `slicer check --json` is clean.

sections.heading: Git
sections.body:
Worktree under `.worktrees/` on a feature branch. No commit unless the owner
asks; no AI attribution.
